newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's five-month trade deficit falls 32 percent.
newsitem.headline: Peru's five-month trade deficit falls 32 percent.

text.p: Peru's trade deficit fell 32 percent in the first five months of 1997 to $566 million from $830 million in the same period last year, the Central Reserve Bank said Friday.

Exports grew 16 percent in the first five months to $2.703 billion, compared with the same period the year before, the bank added in its weekly report. Imports were $3.269 billion in the first five months, up three percent compared with the same period in 1996.
Traditional exports grew 10 percent to $1.884 billion, while non-traditional exports rose 36 percent to $792 million, and the bank's category of "other" exports fell 19 percent to $27 million.

Among imports, consumer goods fell three percent to $708 million, and raw materials fell one percent to $1.332 billion, while capital goods gained 17 percent to $1.139 billion and "other" goods were off 21 percent to $90 million.
Peru's trade deficit fell nine percent in 1996 to $1.996 billion from $2.185 billion in 1995, according to the bank.
